why: XOR cancels pairs again: XOR every number 1..n together with every array element, and each present value appears twice and cancels, leaving the missing one (the sum formula works too, but XOR cannot overflow).
hints: If you XOR 1..n and also XOR the array, how many times does each present value appear?
Twice, so it cancels. The missing value appears only once, in 1..n.
acc = 0; for i in 1..n: acc ^= i; for v in nums: acc ^= v. n = len(nums) + 1. O(n), O(1) space.
pitfalls: n = 1 gives an empty array and the answer 1.
The sum formula n(n+1)/2 can overflow 32-bit integers in other languages.
